To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the LBL stochastic cooling electrodes have been shown to have the required frequency response, and that they are capable of detecting particle displacements in the cooling system.
The frequency response of a single LBL stochastic cooling loop-pair to a wire signal is well represented by the response of a loop-pair with the wire at the mid-plane.

The response of the LBL stripline cooling electrodes to a beam is well represented by the response of a wire simulating the beam; and that the response to the wire is in excellent agreement with the response to a beam, both in magnitude and phase, and in the dependence of the response on the displacement of the wire from the midplane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing the technology for the construction of the TeV-I stochastic cooling system, and with the measurement of the performance of the system.
the measurement of the frequency response of the LBL cooling electrodes, and the results are in good agreement with the design.
the development of a new type of electrode for the stochastic cooling systems in the TeV-I anti-proton accumulator and storage rings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the measurements made on the LBL stochastic cooling arrays were in good agreement with theory and with each other, and that the measurements on the arrays with actual beams were in good agreement, both in magnitude and in phase, with measurements made on the same arrays with wire signals.
the frequency response of the LBL stochastic cooling electrodes is well understood.
the measurements of both single loop-pair response and of the 16 loop-pairs array response were found to be in good agreement with theoretical expectations, and with each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the frequency response of the cooling system is well known.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of using stripline loop pairs to cool a TeV beam.

the measurements made with the wire signal were in good agreement with those made with the actual beam, and that the results of the wire signal measurements were consistent with the results of measurements made at LBL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LBL stochastic cooling arrays are very sensitive, with a noise figure of about 1.6 dB, and have very good beam position sensitivity, about 0.5 mm.
the frequency response of the cooling electrodes is not uniform over the entire frequency band.
the response of the loop-pairs is quite linear, and that the response is quite uniform over a range of 10 cm or so, and that the sum response is very close to that of a single loop-pair.
